newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania relief force to number hundreds-diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Albania relief force to number hundreds-diplomat.

text.p: Foreign nations are discussing a security force of several hundred to protect emergency aid to Albania after armed unrest in Europe's poorest nation, the head of a relief mission said on Wednesday.

Jan de Marchant et d'Ansembourg, a Dutch diplomat, said that the size of any foreign force depended largely on how far Albania would contribute. Asked if it might be several thousand strong, he said: "No, no, we're not talking about thousands in any case. We have not decided anything about numbers but it will not be thousands."

D'Ansembourg arrived in Tirana from Italy at the head of a relief mission of about 15 experts from the 54-nation Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), the European Union and its Commission and the Council of Europe.
He told reporters on arrival that most discussions about sending police or troops were under way with the four Eurofor nations -- France, Italy, Portugal and Spain.
Military experts from the four Eurofor countries, along with representatives from Austria and Greece, arrived on Tuesday to scout out the conditions for a possible force.
D'Ansembourg, heading his second mission in two weeks to Albania, said he would meet Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and other ministers on Thursday to work out details of his visit.
